title: Plane waves on spheres in the time domain: a faint one (εr 1.0001) and a ceramic one (εr 4), radius 5 mm, at 10 GHz, on 0.5 mm cells
source: The Mie series for a sphere of size parameter ka = 1.047 and index √1.0001 and 2: the coefficients aₙ, bₙ and amplitudes S₁, S₂ (C. F. Bohren, D. R. Huffman, Absorption and Scattering of Light by Small Particles, Wiley 1983, §4.4), evaluated by emcraft-theory (which meets their BHMIE listing to 1e-5); σ_sca = (2π/k²) Σ (2n + 1)(|aₙ|² + |bₙ|²), the radar cross-section 4π|S₁|²/k² in the H-plane

quantities.quantity: scattering cross-section of the faint sphere at 10 GHz (mm²)
quantities.reason: a sphere so faint scatters as its volume does (Rayleigh–Gans), so this checks the total-field/scattered-field split, which lets no incident wave leak into the scattered region (the one-dimensional incident grid has the same dispersion as the three-dimensional one along the axis), and the Huygens box in the scattered field: 1.1 % high, the staircased sphere's volume

quantities.quantity: scattering cross-section of the ceramic sphere at 10 GHz (mm²)
quantities.reason: the sphere staircased on 0.5 mm cells and the wave inside it 15 cells to a wavelength (the grid's dispersion slows it): 10.4 % high, where the faint sphere shows the split itself is good to 1 %
